prior_narrative.tldr: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5 and the unguarded Mythos 5 as long-horizon models "made safe for general use," and an early hands-on called Fable "relentlessly proactive." Days later a US export-control directive citing national security suspended all access, framed by outside recaps as temporary; the models then returned only on Amazon Bedrock, gated behind a provider_data_share opt-in that ships prompts and outputs to Anthropic for 30-day retention with human review.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Anthropic is redeploying Claude Fable 5 starting July 1 after the US lifted its export-control directive, shipping updated cybersecurity safeguards and a new industry jailbreak framework alongside the return.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: A frontier tier went from GA launch to a government-ordered suspension, to a conditional data-sharing-only return, to full redeployment inside three weeks — proof that access to a flagship can be revoked or re-priced in data-confidentiality terms with only days of notice.

status.detail: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 launched "made safe for general use," were suspended by a US export-control directive, returned on Amazon Bedrock only under a data-sharing opt-in, and are now being redeployed from July 1 after the controls were lifted, with updated cybersecurity safeguards.

beats.headline: Claude Fable 5 + Mythos 5 ship — "made safe for general use"
beats.summary: Anthropic ships the Mythos-class Fable 5 and the unguarded Mythos 5, billed as made safe for general use.

beats.headline: A powerful but "relentlessly proactive" beast
beats.summary: The first sustained hands-on reads Fable 5 as relentlessly proactive, deploying every trick it knows to reach a goal.

beats.headline: US export-control directive suspends access
beats.summary: Citing national security, the US government orders access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 suspended; coverage recasts the launch as "too dangerous to release."

beats.headline: Reframed as a temporary suspension — no re-enable date
beats.summary: An outside recap ties the takedown to the export-control directive and frames it as temporary rather than permanent.

beats.headline: Back on Bedrock — but only with data-sharing opted in
beats.summary: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 return on Amazon Bedrock gated behind provider_data_share: prompts and outputs go to Anthropic for 30-day retention with human review.

beats.headline: Export controls lifted — redeploying July 1 with new safeguards
beats.summary: With the export directive lifted, Anthropic redeploys Fable 5 from July 1, adding updated cybersecurity safeguards and a new industry jailbreak framework.

open_questions: Does the July 1 redeployment restore standard private-inference terms, or does the Bedrock provider_data_share requirement persist?
What exactly changed in the "updated cybersecurity safeguards" that satisfied the export-control review?
Will the new industry jailbreak framework be adopted by other frontier labs, or is it Anthropic-only?
Is Fable 5 / Mythos 5 redeploying beyond Bedrock — first-party API or other clouds — on private-inference terms?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If you paused Fable 5 / Mythos 5 during the suspension, confirm the July 1 redeploy terms before re-enabling — check whether Bedrock still forces provider_data_share (30-day retention, human review) — and keep a fallback tier wired so a single-flagship dependency can't strand you again.
